The “first railway” depends on how “first” is defined. If considering the earliest public railways using horse or wagon technology, wooden wagonways in Britain date to at least 1725 and horse-drawn railways to 1796 [d2,d6]. If focusing on the first public railway to operate freight and passenger service with steam traction, the Stockton & Darlington Railway in England opened on September 27, 1825 [d3,d7,d8]. Regionally, sources also cite 1848 as the year of the first railways in Spain and South America [d1], and 1826–1827 for early U.S. railroads [d4,d5,d9].
